plugin.name: Certificates
plugin.description: See, issue and renew TLS certificates on your hosts with certbot and acme.sh, and get an alert before they expire.

use.title: Use Certificates
use.description: See certificates on hosts you can reach, and change them on hosts you can edit.

enable.label: Certificates
enable.description: Manage TLS certificates on this host from the Certificates tab.

useSudo.label: Use sudo
useSudo.description: Use sudo to read and change certificates. Turn off if the login is root.

readOnly.label: Read only
readOnly.description: Show certificates but never change them on this host.

expiryWarnDays.label: Warn before expiry
expiryWarnDays.description: Certificates with this many days or fewer left show as expiring and send an alert.

showPanel.label: Show certificates panel in terminals
showPanel.description: Let the certificates panel open beside this host's SSH terminal.

companionAutoOpen.label: Open the certificates panel with new terminals
companionAutoOpen.description: Show the certificates panel beside every SSH terminal that has Certificates on. You can still open and close it from the button on the right edge.

companionSide.label: Certificates panel side
companionSide.description: Where the certificates panel sits next to a terminal.

companionSize.label: Certificates panel size
companionSize.description: Width in pixels, or height when it is at the bottom. You can also drag its edge.

companionEdgeButton.label: Show the panel button
companionEdgeButton.description: Show a small button on the right edge of a terminal that opens the certificates panel.

tab.title: Certificates
tab.error: Could not load certificates from this host.
tab.disabled: Certificates is turned off for this host. Turn it on in the host settings.
tab.sudo: Changes need a root login, passwordless sudo or a saved Sudo Password on this host.

actions.working: Working. This can take a few minutes.

install.title: certbot and acme.sh are not installed on this host
install.hint: Install certbot to get and renew certificates from Let's Encrypt.
install.noManager: No supported package manager was found. Install certbot by hand.
install.desc: This installs certbot with the host's package manager.

certs.renewAllDone: Renewed the certificates that were due.
certs.revokeDesc: The authority marks it as invalid and it is removed from this host. Anything still using it stops working.
certs.deleteDesc: It stays valid but won't renew any more. certbot also deletes its files, acme.sh keeps them.

issue.title: New certificate
issue.working: Asking the authority. This can take a few minutes.
issue.domainsPlaceholder: Type a domain and press Enter
issue.domainsHint: The first one names the certificate.
issue.standaloneHint: Runs a small web server on port 80, so nothing else may use that port.
issue.webrootHint: Puts a file in your web server's folder. The web server keeps running.
issue.dnsHint: Adds a DNS record through your provider's API. Needed for wildcards.
issue.dnsProviderCertbot: The name of an installed certbot DNS plugin, like cloudflare.
issue.dnsProviderAcme: An acme.sh DNS name without dns_, like cf. Its API token must already be set on the host.
issue.credentialsHint: The file on the host with your API token. It is never read by Termix.
issue.emailHint: Optional. The authority uses it for expiry notices.
issue.stagingHint: For testing. The certificate is not trusted, and rate limits are much higher.

inspect.hint: Check what a server sends over TLS, as seen from this host, or read a certificate file on it.
inspect.noOpenssl: openssl is not installed on this host.
inspect.name: Name

renewal.hint: How this host renews certificates on its own. Change it on the host.
renewal.certbotOff: No timer or cron job was found, so certificates won't renew on their own.
renewal.acmeOff: No cron job was found, so certificates won't renew on their own.

watch.start: Alert me before certificates on this host expire
watch.on: You will get an alert before certificates here expire.
watch.off: Alerts for this host are off.

card.title: Certificates
card.empty: Turn on Certificates for a host to see its certificates here.

manager.title: Certificates
manager.disabled: Turn on Certificates for this host in its settings to see them here.
